t66b_secfgallw14:
# How to Forgive Without Forgetting

For many people, healing does get around to some forgiveness eventually, or at least to not being run by the resentment anymore. It can't be put on a schedule (nobody gets a gold star for forgiving fastest). And you don't have to forgive first to get safe, set boundaries, hold someone accountable, get justice or get better. Staying in active resentment has a cost, though: it narrows what you can see, and your little one ends up organized around the injury. Forgiving early because you're pushed to has a cost too. You get a very enlightened-looking performance, and the wound just moves underground.

What can help is seeing how they got there. Picture everything that had made them who they were by that moment, what happened to them and what they learned, the pain they carried and what they could and couldn't handle. From in there, it was the only move they had. Hurt people often pass on pain they never worked through. You may have heard that from somebody telling you to forgive. When you see it for yourself, though, you might find yourself forgiving them, and if you've held them uniquely to blame, the rage can soften into something more accurate.

They still have to answer for what they did, and it still hurt. Seeing how they got there doesn't make it okay, and in theory they could have done something else. It's just that punishing them now can't reach back and give them what they were missing then, the sense to see it or the help. Or the skills. What's left is fixing what can be fixed, and making it easier for something different to happen now. So a boundary can still be right. So can the law, if it comes to that, or telling them plainly it was wrong (or telling yourself, if they'd never hear it). Keeping away from them for good can be right too, and you can still forgive them from over there. "I understand how you became this way" can sit right next to "I now understand why I shouldn't rely on you for this."

Forgiving yourself works the same way. Own what you did (only what was yours), and let yourself feel the remorse. Repair what you can, by apologizing or making amends. Changing the behavior counts too. Then you're allowed to stop holding yourself hostage, and the responsibility stays. If you're thinking "not me, not after what I did," forgiving other people tends to be harder too. Some harms take years, so don't push it. Forgive too soon and it's only a show; stay in the resentment and you end up living there. Every so often, come back to how they got to be someone who could do that, until you understand it well enough that it changes how you feel.
